A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and provide readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–E. Renamed strategies and relocated proofs and figures can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original likelihood-scaling experiments, belief-propagation simulations, L&O-NAE-SAT evaluations, text-generation results, and Sudoku and Zebra experiments.

after.justification: V3 retains those original results and adds LLaDA-8B evaluations on coding, math, MMLU, and ROCStories.

M1.justification: The two confidence-based ordering rules and core training approach are retained; dropping 'K' from their names is cosmetic. Appendix D.3 introduces a limited inference adaptation for the LLaDA application: semi-autoregressive sampling for instruction-answering, while infilling uses non-autoregressive sampling.

E1.justification: V3 adds HumanEval infilling with single-line, multi-line, and split-line scenarios, Math, MMLU, and ROCStories infilling. This substantially extends evaluation beyond the retained synthetic distributions, unconditional text generation, and logic puzzles.

E2.justification: Matched experiments retain the same vanilla MDM, adaptive ordering, and applicable ARM comparators. Table 4 extends the existing vanilla, top-probability, and probability-margin comparison to LLaDA benchmarks; it introduces no additional comparator.

E3.justification: The new LLaDA-8B evaluations introduce a substantially larger test model and task-specific protocols: semi-autoregressive instruction-answering, non-autoregressive infilling, and different output-length rules (Appendix D.3). Existing experimental settings remain stable; the 2048-token length made explicit in the main text was already specified in v1 Appendix C.1.

E4.justification: Appendix D.1.2 adds a brief comparison of deterministic versus binomially sampled numbers of tokens to unmask, reporting comparable generative perplexity without a numerical ablation table. Existing error-imbalance analyses and hard-Sudoku generalization are retained; the belief-propagation analysis is relocated.

E5.justification: The repeated permutation sampling and 1000 masking repetitions in Appendix C are unchanged. V3 adds no seed counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other uncertainty-reporting procedures for its new benchmark results.

E6.justification: V3 Table 4 adds six benchmark columns. For vanilla, top probability, and probability margin respectively, HumanEval-Multi scores are 16.5%, 20.8%, and 25.4%, while Math scores are 28.5%, 31.3%, and 34.3%. The original Tables 1–3, hard-Sudoku results (Table 4 to Table 5), and retained plotted findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: V3 corrects the reverse-kernel mask state from m to 0 and removes the erroneous argmin-of-log assertion. However, its integral loss acquires an extra minus sign inconsistent with the stated decreasing noise schedule and Equation (1). The hardness results and any-order equivalence proof already appear in v1; the revised weights in Proposition 2.1 are algebraically equivalent.

C1.justification: The central training-hardness and adaptive-inference claims, including the Sudoku advantage over ordered ARMs, are retained. The abstract and introduction add explicit effectiveness claims for coding and math on LLaDA-8B and give greater prominence to applicability when generation order varies across sequences.

C2.justification: Section 4.4 extends the uncertainty-based explanation of probability-margin decoding to difficult coding and math tasks. Appendix D.1.2 adds a rationale for matching token counts to training-time masking marginals. The new assertion that both adaptive strategies consistently outperform vanilla inference overstates Table 4, which contains a ROCStories exception.

D1.justification: V3 newly specifies Gaussian oracle noise, deterministic and binomial token-count choices, use of the Ye et al. codebase and defaults, and LLaDA sampling instructions. It removes v1's explicit bidirectional-attention description for puzzle models. These documentation changes do not establish changes to the retained experiments.

R1.justification: V3 adds Nie et al. (2025) for LLaDA and Bavarian et al. (2022) for code infilling, and revises some attribution in the main exposition. Appendix A's research positioning is largely unchanged. Updates to publication years and venues refer to existing works rather than additional literature.

P1.justification: The introduction and Sections 2–3 receive substantial explanatory rewriting, emphasizing known versus sequence-dependent generation order. The lengthy Proposition 3.3 proof outline moves from the main text to Appendix B.3, Appendix E is reorganized, and the ordering strategies are renamed across the main discussion. This substantially revises exposition and narrative structure.

P2.justification: V3 adds a full-width LLaDA results table and moves and enlarges the belief-propagation plot from main-text Figure 3 to appendix Figure 4. The generative-perplexity plot becomes Figure 3, and existing tables and figures are repositioned with terminology updates. The overall visual format remains similar.

improvement.justification: The LLaDA-8B comparisons provide useful evidence that adaptive ordering extends to coding and math, strengthening v1's puzzle and unconditional-text evidence. Added decoding details also improve reproducibility. The net gain is limited by sparse documentation and uncertainty reporting for the new evaluations, the ROCStories exception to claimed consistent improvement (21.10% versus vanilla's 21.23%), and the newly introduced loss-sign inconsistency.
